title: Grateful Dead Live at Dane County Coliseum on 1973-10-25
lineage: SBD Master Reel > ? > DAT > CD-R > EAC (secure) > Cool Edit(minor cleanup) > CDWAV > mkwat > SHN

ai_review.summary: A stellar 10/25/73 soundboard capture with crisp mix and occasional glitches, featuring a smoking China>Rider, monster Dark Star‑Mind‑Left‑Body jam, and transcendent Eyes → Stella.
ai_review.review: The October 25, 1973 show is widely hailed as one of Dick Latvala’s favorites, delivering high‑energy performances of China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider, a sprawling Dark Star/ Mind Left Body sequence, and an unforgettable Eyes of the World into Stella Blue.  The SBD source sounds generally clear and balanced, though listeners note some tape‑hisses, pops, clipping on the bass and a missing segment of the Dark Star jam.  Overall the musical payoff outweighs the technical flaws, making this a must‑have for any 1973 Dead collection.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 20 reviews overwhelmingly praise the performance and only note moderate recording issues; the strong show weight (70%) pushes the overall rating into the high‑four range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally crisp SBD mix with occasional hiss, pops and a few clipping artifacts on the bass.  Several reviewers report missing or patched sections (notably a chunk of Dark Star) and minor drop‑outs, but overall the recording is listenable and captures the band’s dynamics.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
Dark Star > Mind Left Body Jam > Dark Star
Weather Report Suite Prelude > Part I > L.I.G. > G.D.T.R.F.B.
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds solidly with strong Bertha, HCS and Playin', while the second set launches into a monster sequence of China>Rider, the expansive Dark Star suite and a soaring Eyes → Stella that defines the evening.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s solos are highlighted as soulful (Eyes) and powerful (Stella), with his tone described as “perfect” and “nails it.”
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass is praised for its scary depth in Dark Star, standout licks at the end of Eyes, and overall ‘bomb’ quality throughout the jam sections.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir receives nods for solid rhythm work behind Jerry, especially on Bertha and early set songs.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith (and later Brent) are lauded for “magic droplets” of keyboards that complement the jams, with several reviewers calling his playing a highlight of the show.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drumming is noted as strong and in shape; occasional clipping on bass is mentioned but drums remain solid throughout.
